objective: Provide a provider-neutral cross-agent handoff receipt admission primitive that binds agent identity, delegated scope, generation, freshness, approval, trust, trace position, result linkage, replay protection, and explicit non-authority semantics without executing remote work or minting authority.

features: provider-neutral source and target agent identity binding
capability-scope subset and policy allowlist enforcement
generation fencing and bounded TTL freshness checks
operator approval requirement for privileged handoff scope
verified result admission with handoff/result digest linkage
tamper detection for admitted handoff records and result linkage
explicit model-output, provider-metadata, handoff, and result non-authority boundaries

research_inputs.finding: The Agent2Agent protocol defines provider-neutral agent discovery, task-oriented interactions, streaming or polling task state, and explicit artifact-oriented exchanges between independent agents.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: Handoff receipts bind source and target identity, task/objective scope, generation, trace position, and result linkage while keeping protocol metadata outside the authority boundary.

research_inputs.finding: The Agents SDK documents handoffs, guardrails, approvals, sessions, tracing, MCP tool calling, and resumable agent state as runtime composition mechanisms.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL separates handoff admission from execution, requires explicit policy and approval, and records deterministic receipt evidence independent of a provider SDK.

research_inputs.finding: The memory-poisoning study identifies persistent memory and multiple write channels as cross-session attack surfaces that require provenance and trust controls.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: Remote model/provider results are quarantined by default and cannot become execution authority merely through a cross-agent handoff.

research_inputs.finding: Context engineering recommends bounded, high-signal context assembly and separation of instructions from external data.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: Handoff receipts expose bounded, policy-checked evidence and retain explicit non-authority semantics for delegated content and results.

limitations: The implementation is a bounded userspace/control-plane admission contract and does not contact remote agents, execute delegated tasks, mint credentials, or provide network transport, PKI, or distributed consensus.

Identity, trust, approval evidence, and provider metadata are caller-supplied inputs; this local contract does not provide hardware attestation, independent signatures, or external identity verification.
The benchmark measures local Python control-plane overhead and excludes network, storage, model, accelerator, and kernel latency.

The validation used deterministic local fixtures and does not qualify physical GPUs or NPUs, TPM or secure-enclave keys, production KMS, independent builders, live multi-host deployment, or external security review.
This evidence does not claim AGI capability, production approval, superiority to Linux, independent qualification, or completion of the existing external release blockers.
